rules.title: Semantic HTML
rules.what: Use semantic elements (nav, main, button, table) rather than div/span + JS replicas; a native element carries the accessibility contract for free.
rules.why: A native button is focusable, keyboard-operable, screen-reader-announced and zero-JS; a div+JS replica must reimplement all four, and usually only does two.
rules.how: Default to semantic elements; ARIA only on top of semantics that the platform cannot express; validate with keyboard and screen reader passes.

patterns.note: div with a button/link role; a native element is usually the fix.

verify.how: Keyboard journey works on native semantics; automated a11y checks run on the result.

rules.title: Media with explicit dimensions and lazy loading
rules.what: img/video carry width and height (or aspect-ratio) and loading="lazy" when below the fold; no layout-shifting media.
rules.why: Missing dimensions force a layout shift on every late-loading image (wasted reflow) and a lower CLS; lazy loading keeps below-the-fold bytes off the first paint entirely.
rules.how: width/height attributes on the media elements, loading=lazy + decoding=async below the fold, aspect-ratio in CSS for fluid layouts.

patterns.note: img without dimensions; candidate for layout shift.

verify.how: Audited pages: media elements carry dimensions; CLS within budget.

rules.title: Forms: labels, autocomplete, validation
rules.what: Every input has a label, relevant autocomplete attributes, and inline validation; forms never lose user input on failure.
rules.why: A form that loses input or is inaccessible wastes every byte spent reaching it, and the user's whole effort - the most expensive failure of all (NR-UX-006).
rules.how: label for=, input autocomplete=, client validation with server confirmation, preserved values on error.

patterns.note: Input with no label, aria-label or bindable id; candidate for a missing label.

verify.how: Failing submission keeps input and reports field-level errors; keyboard-only completion works.

rules.title: Modern layout over hacks
rules.what: Use flexbox/grid for layout; no float hacks, no presentational divs, no CSS table displays for layout.
rules.why: Layout hacks add wrapper nodes and CSS workarounds the browser must reconcile on every layout pass; native layout properties express the same intent with less code and better reflow cost.
rules.how: Grid for two-dimensional, flex for one-dimensional, gap instead of margin hacks; remove the wrappers the old hack required.

patterns.note: Float used for layout; candidate for flex/grid migration.
CSS table for layout; modern layout usually expresses it better.

verify.how: Stylesheet review: no layout floats outside documented legacy scope.

limits: Email templates and legacy browsers constrain layout tools; document the scope.

rules.title: System fonts or subset web fonts
rules.what: Prefer system font stacks; when a brand font is required, subset it, limit weights, self-host with preload on the critical one and font-display: swap.
rules.why: Web fonts block or shift text rendering and transfer tens to hundreds of KB per weight; system fonts cost nothing and never flash. Subsetting removes the glyphs the page never displays.
rules.how: font-family stacks with named system fallbacks; unicode-range subsetting (latin + used glyphs), 2-3 weights maximum, swap + preload for the critical file.

patterns.note: Google Fonts tag/link; check subsetting, weight count, self-hosting trade-off.

verify.how: Font inventory: families, weights, subsets, loading strategy, fallbacks; text renders without long invisible period.

limits: Brand fonts are legitimate; the rule bounds their cost.

rules.title: Declare the page language, work without optional JavaScript
rules.what: Every document declares its language (<html lang>) and its essential content and controls work before, or without, non-essential JavaScript.
rules.why: Screen readers pick pronunciation from lang; a page that needs a large script before showing anything excludes slow devices, slow networks and assistive tools first.
rules.how: <html lang="fr"> (and lang on passages in another language); server-rendered content and native forms; scripts deferred for enhancements only.

verify.how: Page checked with JavaScript disabled for the essential task; automated check confirms lang is set.

rules.title: Cheap animations, honoured preferences
rules.what: Animate only transform and opacity, avoid infinite decorative animations and broad will-change, and stop motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
rules.why: Animating layout properties forces reflow at every frame; continuous animations keep the GPU busy and can trigger vestibular disorders.
rules.how: transition: transform .2s, opacity .2s; will-change set on the element just before it animates; @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; }.

patterns.note: transition: all animates every property, layout included.
Infinite animation; check it is essential and stops under reduced motion.

verify.how: Performance panel shows no layout per animation frame; reduced-motion setting stops the animations.

rules.title: Media and container queries before layout scripts
rules.what: When JavaScript recalculates layout on resize, check whether media or container queries give the same behaviour for the supported browsers.
rules.why: Resize handlers that measure and restyle the DOM cost script and layout work at every event; CSS queries are resolved by the engine.
rules.how: @container and @media rules; ResizeObserver only for what CSS cannot express.

verify.how: Resize trace compared before/after; layout result identical on the supported browsers.
